title: The IRS Double-Taxes Your Social Security — $84K Gone
hook: You paid into Social Security your whole career — then the IRS taxes up to 85% of what you collect, money you already paid taxes on once.
angle: The 1983 income thresholds that were never adjusted for inflation now trap 56% of Social Security recipients in a tax most retirees never saw coming.
audience: Pre-retirees 50-65 and current retirees who don't realize they owe income tax on SS benefits
key_numbers: 85% max taxable portion of SS benefits
56% of recipients now pay the tax (was only 10% in 1983)
$4,200 average annual extra tax for affected retirees
